newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil markets quiet, steady, barges gain $1.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil markets quiet, steady, barges gain $1.

text.p: NWE fuel oil markets were stable on Tuesday, apart from high sulphur barges, which gained on bunker demand.
Prices for high sulphur barges jumped $1 to $84/$85 fob ARA. One barge trade for prompt material was heard done at $85.50 while most other business was in the $84 to $85 range.
High sulphur cargoes were idle, with little end-user interest and most focus on the Portugese tender, whose result is due on Wednesday.
Low sulphur markets were again quiet, with little demand, but prices holding up well in the face of crude's fall.
Ample availability was reported for second half April.
"It's looking toppy and I don't see what there is to support it," said one trader, who saw the product capped by price weakness in the straight-run grade.
Dealers were similarly negative about high sulphur's near-term value.
"There's nothing going on in the north. It's a bit confused and we expect it to weaken," said a trader.
